da40e6bd4159aea0da00c8b497d1905d24d40850: Glungezer is a small, understated resort — 23 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where people come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. Glungezer's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. Glungezer's altitude (950 m at the base, 2304 m at the top) helps it maintain decent snow cover in the depths of winter. January and February are the most reliable months; in December and March, it is worth checking conditions before finalising a booking. The day lift pass at €50 places Glungezer in the intermediate category on budget — neither cheap nor exorbitant. The quality of the ski area and its facilities justifies this price for most skiers. In short: Glungezer does not compete with the ski giants, and does not pretend to. It is an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.

da581d8ed555005703599e24a4a2aa6427faa084: A resort on a human scale, La Chapelle d'Abondance focuses on the quality of its welcome and its closeness rather than on impressive figures. Its 40 km of runs are perfect for a stay of 3 to 4 days, especially for families or skiers who don't need to keep changing their terrain. La Chapelle d'Abondance's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, a well-run childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. The altitude of La Chapelle d'Abondance (1010 m at the bottom, 2000 m at the top) allows it to maintain decent snow cover in mid-winter. January and February are the most reliable months; in December and March, it is worth checking conditions before finalising a booking. The budget for a stay in La Chapelle d'Abondance is clearly high: €68 for a day pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence – but you should be aware of it before you go. In short: La Chapelle d'Abondance is one of those rare resorts that combines a real village, a sincerely family atmosphere and runs suited to everyone. It's hard to get your stay wrong here.

dad1d99ef549dbbca87bf42b9cb9946b18a806e0: Valmorel and Saint-François-Longchamp join up via the Col de la Madeleine, forming 165 km of runs between Tarentaise and Maurienne. Valmorel is a case apart in the Alps: built in 1976, it deliberately rejected concrete in favour of a fully pedestrian village of timber and lauze stone, with painted façades and a central shopping street — an architectural gamble that has aged rather well. Saint-François-Longchamp, on the Maurienne side, is sunnier and more low-key. The area is particularly well suited to families and intermediate skiers, with a majority of blue runs and excellent value for money.
